title: IntentCLI.swift:131 assigns the console tail's lifecycle to a verb that does not exist
body:
**`IntentCLI.swift:131` HANDS THE CONSOLE TAIL'S LIFECYCLE TO A VERB THAT DOES NOT EXIST.** The doc comment on `IntentCLI.stream` reads, in the present tense and as a settled division of responsibility:

> `onStart` receives a handle so a caller can end the child early -- the console's tail, whose pipeline the verb owns and takes down on SIGTERM (the verb's job, not the app's).

**DRIVEN, WITH THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST.** `intent --help | grep -ci daemon` returns 2, so the probe can see a verb when one is there. Over the full surface it returns nothing for `log`, `tail` or `console`: not among the top-level verbs, not under `daemon` (`start stop restart status run help`), not under `app` (`start stop restart status help`). **There is no verb to own the pipeline and no verb to take it down.**

**WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A COMMENT TO FIX.** The sentence does not read as a plan. It reads as an already-settled allocation, and the party it allocates to is absent. **Whoever arrives to build the console reads it, concludes the tail's lifecycle is handled elsewhere, and builds on it** -- which produces exactly the leaked-`tail`-per-open-and-close that `ST0064` `AC-01.4` exists to prevent, reached by believing a true-sounding sentence rather than by neglect. `AC-01.4`'s own framing is that the leak is invisible to the operator and unbounded in count: the machine gets slower over a week and nothing ever points at the menubar.

**SECOND HALF: I INFERRED THE MECHANISM WRONG, MEASURED IT, AND THE CORRECTED PICTURE IS SHARPER THAN THE GUESS.** This filing first said, flagged as inference: _Foundation's `Process` does not start a new process group, so a child inherits the app's and a SIGKILL to the app never reaches it._ **MEASURED AND FALSE.** A compiled Swift probe -- parent identity printed before any spawn, so there is no ambiguity about who the parent is -- gives `parent pid=80915 pgid=78277` and `child pid=80920 pgid=80920 ppid=80915`. **The child's pgid equals its own pid: Foundation makes it a NEW PROCESS GROUP LEADER**, and it does not inherit the app's group.

**THE HAZARD SURVIVES AND CHANGES SHAPE, WHICH IS WHY THE MEASUREMENT WAS WORTH TAKING.** Being in its OWN group means the child is MORE isolated from the app, not less: a signal sent to the app's group never reaches it, so killing the app -- SIGKILL included -- leaves the child running by construction rather than by oversight. And `RunningProcess.terminate()` (`IntentCLI.swift:269`) is `process.terminate()`, which signals **the child's PID and not its group**, so a `tail` spawned by the verb survives even an ORDERLY stop.

**AND THE MEASUREMENT NAMES THE REMEDY, WHICH THE INFERENCE COULD NOT HAVE.** Because the child is a group LEADER, its pgid is well-defined and equal to its pid, so `kill(-pgid, SIGTERM)` is available and reaches the whole pipeline. **A fix built on my original inference would have been aimed at the wrong mechanism entirely.**

**MEASURED, SEPARATELY, AND UNCHANGED BY THE ABOVE:** `runProcessStreaming` (`IntentCLI.swift:215`) is a plain `Process` with a `Pipe`, `try process.run()` and `waitUntilExit()` -- no `setpgid`, no group signalling, no signal handling anywhere in the file. `AC-01.4`'s own framing stands: a handler that cleans up on SIGTERM and SIGINT proves nothing about SIGKILL, which cannot be handled at all, so the orphan must be prevented by construction. **What the build has is the group; what it lacks is anything that signals it.**

**THE CONSTRAINT ON ANY REMEDY, AND IT IS THE PART THAT GOES INVISIBLE ONCE THE MEASUREMENT IS COLD (vc, 2026-09-08).** `kill(-pgid, SIGTERM)` reaches the pipeline ONLY BECAUSE the child is a group leader, so its pgid is well-defined and equals its pid. **Nothing pins that.** It is not a documented Foundation guarantee -- it is what a probe measured of the Foundation on this machine, on this day.

**IF A FUTURE FOUNDATION STOPS MAKING THE CHILD A LEADER, THE CHILD INHERITS THE APP'S GROUP AND `-pgid` NAMES THE APP.** The remedy then does not degrade to doing nothing: **it degrades to signalling the app itself, which is worse than the leak it was written to fix.**

**SO WHATEVER FIXTURE EVENTUALLY HOLDS THE GROUP-SIGNALLING BEHAVIOUR MUST ASSERT `child.pgid == child.pid` FIRST, as the precondition the remedy RESTS ON, before asserting anything about the pipeline dying.** **A test that only checks the tail is gone passes on a build that killed the app** -- both leave no `tail` running, and only one of them is the fix.

**CURRENT REACH OF THE TRAP.** Nothing calls `IntentCLI.stream` today -- re-driven on the PUBLIC symbol after I first probed the private `runProcessStreaming`, which could not have answered the caller question in either direction. So nothing leaks yet. **The trap is in the prose, and it is live for the next reader rather than for the current build.**

**THE REMEDY HAS BEEN IN THE TREE SINCE 2026-08-26 AND NOTHING LINKED IT (found 2026-09-08 while re-syncing `ST0064`'s docs to the build).** `intent/st/ST0064/design-menubar-app.md` is Geodica's handoff, parked verbatim, and it is where `AC-01.4` and the `IntentCLI.swift:131` comment both come from. It records the identical failure, already diagnosed and already fixed, in their estate:

> Killing the tail child does not work the way you expect. Our `cms logs` is `tail -f | grep` under `sh`, under the BEAM, under a bash dispatcher. `Process.terminate()` from Swift reaches only the top of that chain and leaves orphaned tails behind. Worse, we discovered the CLI verb had been leaking a tail on EVERY exit, including plain ctrl-c at a terminal, **because the BEAM starts port programs in their own process group so no signal ever reached them.**
>
> The fix belongs in the CLI, not the app: **the verb runs its pipeline under a shell that reads its own stdin and takes the process group down when that pipe closes** -- the runtime's death closes it, however it dies. Verified against SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGKILL: zero orphans, where every previous run leaked one. Then the app needs no special handling at all -- plain `terminate()` works.

**THREE THINGS FALL OUT OF THAT AND ALL OF THEM WERE AVAILABLE BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN.**

**ONE: the comment is not an invention, it is a FAITHFUL CARRY-FORWARD.** *The verb's job, not the app's* restates Geodica's *the fix belongs in the CLI, not the app* almost word for word. **The lesson crossed estates and the implementation did not**, which is a more specific defect than a comment being wrong, and a more likely one to recur -- a handoff transfers prose at no cost and code at full cost.

**TWO: it corroborates the process-group measurement from a different runtime.** Geodica hit it because the BEAM starts port programs in their own group; this estate's probe found Foundation makes the child its own group leader. **Same observable, two unrelated runtimes** -- which makes it a property of the pattern rather than a quirk of either.

**THREE: it names a remedy that does not depend on the Foundation property this filing warns about.** A pipeline held under a shell reading its own stdin dies when the pipe closes, **whatever the process group turns out to be** -- so it does not degrade into signalling the wrong group the way `kill(-pgid)` can. It also puts the fix where `AC-01.4` says it belongs, in the verb, and Geodica verified it against all three signals rather than the two that can be handled.

**REMEDY IS NOT OBVIOUS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED HERE.** Either the verb gets built and earns the sentence, or the sentence stops allocating and states the gap, or the app takes the job with process-group construction. That is a design call and it belongs with `AC-01.4`'s owner rather than in a filing.

---

## DISPOSITIONED 2026-09-09 (vc, under the pen delegated by hv 2026-08-21): OPTION (i) -- THE VERB RUNS ITS PIPELINE UNDER A SHELL THAT READS ITS OWN STDIN

**The remedy belongs to the VERB, which is where `AC-01.4` already said it belonged, and the app then needs no special handling: plain `terminate()` works.** ic proposed three options and recommended this one; the recommendation is adopted **on its argument rather than on its authority**, and the argument is recorded here because the argument is the transferable part.

**THE DECIDING ASYMMETRY: (i) REMOVES A PRECONDITION, (iii) PINS ONE.** Option (iii) -- the app takes the job with `kill(-pgid, SIGTERM)` -- works only because a probe measured `child.pgid == child.pid` on this Foundation, on this machine, on one day. **That is not a documented guarantee.** If a future Foundation stops making the child a group leader, the child inherits the app's process group and `-pgid` names **THE APP**. So (iii) does not degrade to doing nothing; **it degrades to killing the application, which is strictly worse than the leak it was written to fix.** A pipeline held under a shell reading its own stdin dies when that pipe closes whatever the process group turns out to be, so (i) needs no such assertion at all.

**A CONSTRAINT THAT RIDES ANY FUTURE MOVE TOWARD GROUP SIGNALLING, RECORDED EVEN THOUGH (i) DOES NOT NEED IT.** Should anyone later reach for (iii), every fixture must assert `child.pgid == child.pid` **FIRST**, before asserting anything about the pipeline dying -- because **a test that only checks the tail is gone PASSES ON A BUILD THAT KILLED THE APP.** Both outcomes leave no tail running and only one of them is the fix. That is a test-design trap worth more than this issue and it is the reason this paragraph is here rather than in a chat message.

**OPTION (ii) IS REJECTED AS A DESTINATION, NOT AS AN OBSERVATION.** It is true that nothing calls `IntentCLI.stream` today and therefore nothing leaks yet. But the defect this issue records is that `IntentCLI.swift:131` allocates a job **in the present tense, as a settled division of responsibility**, to a verb that does not exist -- so the trap is live for the next reader rather than for the current build. Correcting the sentence without building the verb leaves `AC-01.4` unsatisfiable and the allocation merely reworded.

**THE FINDING THAT IS LARGER THAN THE RULING, AND IT IS ic's.** Geodica's estate had this exact failure **already diagnosed AND already fixed** -- verified there against SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGKILL with zero orphans where every previous run leaked one -- and the parked handoff carrying it is in this tree at `intent/st/ST0064/design-menubar-app.md`. **What crossed estates was the sentence and not the code.** The comment at `:131` is a faithful carry-forward of Geodica's *"the fix belongs in the CLI, not the app"*, and it arrived sounding settled. **A handoff transfers prose at no cost and code at full cost, so the prose arrives describing a world the receiving estate does not have.**

**THAT IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS IN A SINGLE EVENING (2026-09-09), WHICH IS WHY IT IS RECORDED AS A CLASS:** a ruling whose only home was a doc comment (`ST0065` ruling 3); a landed ruling still reading as owed in four documents (`ST0065`'s three, against `wp list ST0065` showing `WP-02 Cancelled`); and this -- a fix that travelled as a claim. **In all three the record and the reality disagree, everything reads as current, and nothing in the tooling reports the gap.** See also `0296`, which is the same shape one layer down in the work-package surface.

**IMPLEMENTATION IS ic's AND IS UNBLOCKED BY THIS ENTRY. `ST0064/AC-01.4` releases on it.** `AC-01.7` remains hv's -- Apple Developer credentials are an ACTION on the outside world and no amount of delegated authority substitutes for one.


---

**RULED 2026-09-09 (vc, under hv's pen): OPTION (i) -- THE VERB RUNS ITS PIPELINE UNDER A SHELL THAT READS ITS OWN STDIN**, so the process group goes down when that pipe closes, however the runtime dies. This is Geodica's remedy, already recorded in this estate at `intent/st/ST0064/design-menubar-app.md` and verified in their estate against SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGKILL with zero orphans where every previous run leaked one.

**THE MENU, AND WHAT DECIDED IT.** (i) shell-holds-the-pipeline **CHOSEN**; (ii) the sentence stops allocating and states the gap, declined -- honest, and it leaves `AC-01.4` with no remedy; (iii) the app takes the job with `kill(-pgid, SIGTERM)`, declined.

**THE DECIDING ASYMMETRY IS THAT (i) REMOVES A PRECONDITION WHERE (iii) PINS ONE.** (iii) works only because a probe measured `child.pgid == child.pid` on one Foundation, on one machine, on one day, with no documented guarantee behind it. **If a future Foundation stops making the child a group leader, `-pgid` names the APP -- so (iii) does not degrade to doing nothing, it degrades to KILLING THE APP, which is worse than the leak it was written to fix.** A remedy whose failure mode is worse than its bug is not a remedy. (i) needs no such property: a pipeline held under a shell reading its own stdin dies when the pipe closes whatever the group turns out to be. (i) also puts the fix where `AC-01.4` says it belongs -- in the verb -- after which the app needs no special handling and plain `terminate()` works.

**THE CONSTRAINT RIDES THE RULING EVEN THOUGH (i) DOES NOT NEED IT, because it must survive whichever way anyone later goes.** Any future work that reaches for group signalling **asserts `child.pgid == child.pid` FIRST**, as the precondition the remedy rests on, before asserting anything about the pipeline dying. **A test that only checks the tail is gone PASSES ON A BUILD THAT KILLED THE APP** -- both leave no `tail` running, and only one of them is the fix. That is a test-design trap worth more than this issue.

**AND THE FINDING IS BIGGER THAN THE RULING, SO IT IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT IN THE IMPLEMENTATION.** Geodica had this diagnosed **and fixed**. What crossed estates was the sentence and not the code, and it arrived at `IntentCLI.swift:131` **in the present tense, sounding settled**, allocating a job to a verb that does not exist.

> **A handoff transfers prose at no cost and code at full cost, so the prose arrives describing a world the receiving estate does not have.**

**THAT IS A CLASS AND IT WAS MET FOUR TIMES ON 2026-09-09 ALONE**: a ruling living only in prose while four documents said it was unmade; a landed answer still reading as owed; a fix that travelled as a claim (this one); and `init.rs`'s `NotByInit` reasons allocating template laydown to `intent lang init`, a verb that EXISTS and does not do it (`ST0065` `_catalogue-wp01.md` section 9). **In every instance the allocation sits in a comment, a reason string or a note -- the surface nothing executes, and therefore the surface nothing checks.**

**STILL OPEN: the ruling is made, the remedy is not built.** `AC-01.4` remains unsatisfied and `ST0064` reads 7/9.
